A father's six-year wait for an FIR finally ended when the Bombay High Court ordered a CBI probe into the death of Disha Salian  and the FIR that followed names some of Maharashtra's most prominent political and police figures for investigation. In this piece, I look at what the court actually ordered, what remains allegation versus established fact, and why the RG Kar case in Kolkata (and cases like Unnao, Hathras, and Kathua before it) reveal a troubling pan-India pattern: it's often not the crime but the institutional cover-up around it that proves hardest to prosecute. My full analysis below  written with the sub judice status of these matters firmly in mind.
